title: Same Fix, Different Weights: Replicating Weight-Space Programming with Claude
read_level: partial (full read of abstract, Secs 1-4, 6, 7.3, 8, 10-12 and Exp 5 results; Sec 5 reading-probe details and appendices skimmed via search)
why_wsp: Pre-registered replication of all eight Takehi et al. probes with Claude Opus 5.5 reading, repairing, writing (policies, 1.48M-param Go net) and editing (Qwen3.5-0.8B) network weights as text or via sandboxed tensor tools, without gradients.
domain: RL control (Gymnasium, ALE Atari RAM), 9x9 Go, DDPM shapes, char-LMs, LLM sycophancy (Gemma 3 270M), LLM math reasoning (Qwen3.5-0.8B)
editor: Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5, adaptive thinking, effort high)
target: PPO MLP policies (1,476 to 13,586 weights), DDPMs (28,000), char-LM middle blocks (7,097,856), Go net (1,480,274), Gemma 3 270M finetunes (100,325,376 trainable), Qwen3.5-0.8B (752,393,024 LM params)
interface: direct values (weights pasted into prompt, Exp 1, 1b, 2, 4, 5); code/tensor tools (sandboxed Python, Exp 3, 5b, 6, 7, 8)
loop: one-shot (Exp 1-5, Go budget 0) and closed-loop with feedback (5b rollouts; Go 10/25/50 batches; Qwen 10/25/50 forward passes of 64 problems)

headline_results.claim: Qwen3.5-0.8B MATH-500 raised to 51.4/55.2/58.1% with 10/25/50 passes
headline_results.quote: Claude raised its MATH-500 score from 6.7% to 51.4%, 55.2% and 58.1% (500 problems × 4 samples; at 50 passes +51.4 points, 95% interval [47.9, 55.0]

headline_results.claim: About a third of math gain and nearly all IFEval gain is temperature
headline_results.quote: Temperature alone lifts MATH-500 to 22.1% (s = 0.6) and 20.9% (s = 0.68), about a third of the gain (28–35%)

headline_results.claim: Edits act at output side, not internal loop direction
headline_results.quote: Unlike the original, which removed an internal loop direction, every edit acted at the output: it scaled the final norm ... and the logits of "Wait" and </think>.
it moved the score from 9.2% to 8.3%, a change of −0.8 points [−1.9, +0.2]

headline_results.quote: Claude wrote a network that won 93.8% (Wilson 0.88–0.97) and 87.5% (0.81–0.92) against the two small networks and 85.2% (0.78–0.90) against the equal-sized one.

headline_results.claim: Zero-shot policies beat PPO-100k on 4 of 5 environments
headline_results.quote: the median network beat PPO-100k on 4 of 5 environments (CartPole, MountainCar, LunarLander, Breakout

headline_results.quote: it picked the sycophantic Gemma 3 270M finetune from weights alone in 6/6 runs, with the frozen embedding and vocabulary provided

baselines_and_controls: untrained networks; hidden-unit permutations; hand transcript audits; PPO at 100k/1M/final; Gymnasium heuristic and velocity-push heuristic; heuristic Go bot; norm-only temperature control for Qwen; Gemma 3 270M non-looping control; pre-registered GRADING.md per experiment
runs_and_variance: 3-5 attempts per network in most probes; 1 run per budget in Exp 5b, 6, 8; Wilson and bootstrap 95% intervals; "Five attempts at effort high are therefore fewer independent samples than they look" (Sec 10)
robustness_of_edits: held-out seeds/opening seeds and benchmark evaluation only; fine-tuning/quantization not tested; Qwen edits cast to bf16 with lost-to-rounding elements recorded
verification: pre-registered grading rules (not externally timestamped); permutation equivalence asserted numerically (max logit diff < 1e-5); edited Qwen tensors verified bit-identical elsewhere; paired bootstrap intervals
memorization_vs_reasoning: Extensive: training-data answers follow priors (interface shape, dataset defaults, famous games); repairs and zero-shot policies recall known controllers (LQR, Gymnasium heuristic(), AtariARI annotations); memorisation flag fired on MountainCar and LunarLander; with rollout feedback LunarLander moved off the memorised heuristic; Go nets judged "the least memorised artefact".
limitations_stated: small samples and correlated attempts; design leaks (interface shapes, embedding provided in Exp 7); lenient grading rules; weak Go/PPO baselines; reliance on recalled annotations/heuristics; different environments from original; one model/effort; single-person audits; pre-registration not externally deposited; Exp 8: one run per budget, temperature confound, activation summaries gave extra info, protocol changes.
notes_for_survey: Most complete independent replication of the original WSP probes, with pre-registration and controls; replicates the Qwen MATH-500 headline by its own rule but via output-side edits with a quantified temperature component. Raises the definitional question of whether a weight edit equivalent to a sampling change counts as WSP.
